Communication Networks and Protocols

通信网络与协议

How do you know what's going on in someone's mind? You ask them. You might simply say, "I believe something is troubling you, and sharing it might help to take the burden off your mind." This is a simple exchange of words that we call communication. There can be different ways to communicate. For example, in this scenario, the conversation might have happened in person or via a messaging application or a phone call in a language you both understand. We very briefly introduced you to the concept of communication in Chapter 1. In this chapter, we'll extend the idea of communication in much more detail.

你怎么知道别人心里在想什么？你问他们。你可能只是说：“我觉得有件事在困扰你，说出来也许能帮你卸下心头的负担。”这就是一次简单的言语交流，我们称之为通信。通信可以有不同方式。例如，在这个场景中，对话可能是面对面进行的，也可能通过消息应用或电话、用你们都懂的某种语言进行。我们在第 1 章非常简略地向你介绍了通信的概念。在本章中，我们将更详细地拓展通信这一概念。

The internet has changed a lot over time, and many solutions have been built to solve new problems that we encounter while communicating over the internet. It is important that there are guidelines or mechanisms to ensure that people and machines can work with one another. We'll begin our discussion with communication models to strengthen our understanding of communication over the internet adhering to certain rules, which are called protocols. You may have seen a lot of keywords floating around, such as TCP, XMPP, WebSockets, WebRTC, HTTP, GraphQL, REST, and so on. It can be very confusing to figure out what these terms mean and in which scenarios they should be used. This chapter will help you gain an understanding of communication-related terms, and we'll identify the correct scenarios for using a particular technology.

互联网随时间发生了很大变化，人们构建了许多解决方案来解决在互联网上通信时遇到的新问题。重要的是要有一些准则或机制，确保人和机器能够协同工作。我们将从通信模型开始讨论，以加深我们对互联网上遵循特定规则（这些规则称为协议）进行通信的理解。你可能见过很多满天飞的关键词，例如 TCP、XMPP、WebSockets、WebRTC、HTTP、GraphQL、REST 等等。要弄清楚这些术语是什么意思、应该在哪些场景中使用，可能非常令人困惑。本章将帮助你理解与通信相关的术语，并为特定技术识别正确的使用场景。

Communication Models and Protocols

The first thing that you need to communicate with another person is a common language that you both can understand and use to convey your messages. This common language has a set of rules, generally referred to as grammar, and these rules define how you speak and write. A similar analogy applies in machines: for machines to communicate over the internet, they follow certain rules, referred to as

与另一个人通信，你首先需要一种你们都能理解、用来传达信息的共同语言。这种共同语言有一套规则，通常称为语法，这些规则定义了你如何说和写。类似的类比也适用于机器：机器要在互联网上通信，它们遵循某些规则，称为

Page 159

communication protocols. There are different communication protocols operating at different layers in the communication model. The layers in a communication model represent how data travels from one location to another across the internet in a reliable way. The layers also ensure that data transforms from one form to another so that it can be understood by both humans and machines. We'll talk about two such models—Open Systems Interconnection (OSI) and Transmission Control Protocol and Internet Protocol (TCP/IP)—and then we'll discuss the protocols.

通信协议。在通信模型的不同层上运行着不同的通信协议。通信模型中的层表示数据如何以可靠的方式从互联网上的一个地点传到另一个地点。这些层还确保数据从一种形式转换为另一种形式，以便人和机器都能理解。我们将讨论两种这样的模型——开放式系统互联（OSI）和传输控制协议/网际协议（TCP/IP）——然后再讨论协议。

OSI Model

The OSI model is a reference model that divides the communication network into seven layers, with each layer responsible for performing a specific job. The top layer is an application layer (L7), and the bottommost layer is a physical layer (L1). L7 corresponds to data on how humans perceive, such as plain English language, and L1 corresponds to data on how machines perceive, such as binary format. For any communication to happen, the data travels through the OSI model layers from top to bottom and bottom to top, as described in Table 6-1.

OSI 模型是一个参考模型，它把通信网络划分为七层，每层负责执行一项特定工作。最顶层是应用层（L7），最底层是物理层（L1）。L7 对应人类感知的数据形式，例如普通英文；L1 对应机器感知的数据形式，例如二进制格式。要进行任何通信，数据都会从上到下、再从下到上穿过 OSI 模型各层，如表 6-1 所述。

We'll explore the example protocols in Table 6-1 in the following sections.

我们将在后续各节中探讨表 6-1 中的示例协议。

Table 6-1. OSI model
Layer numberLayer nameLayer function
Layer 7Application layerL7 has direct access to the user data, and the software application relies on it via protocols like HTTP, SMTP, SSH, and so on. This layer is also helpful in service advertisement, such as which services are available over the network to connect.
Layer 6Presentation layerThis layer is responsible for formatting, encryption, decryption, and compression of data. Formatting ensures that L6 is able to format the data as expected by L7. If the data is in encrypted format, L6 decrypts the data before passing it on to L7 or encrypts the data before passing it on to L5 (if encryption is a requirement). To reduce the data footprint, L6 compresses the data before passing it on to L5.
Layer 5Session layerThis layer is responsible for the session lifecycle: initiation, maintenance, and termination.
Layer 4Transportation layerThis layer is responsible for data transport between the devices via protocols like TCP and UDP. It also helps with data buffering, error control, and windowing. It figures out an optimal speed for data communication between the sender and receiver so that a receiver with a slow connection receives the data at the required speed. The extra data can be buffered in a buffer queue so that it can be delivered at the speed needed. In case the buffer queue is full, the new data segments are dropped, referred to as tail drop. The layer can request data retransmission if any data segments are lost to ensure reliable connection in the case of the TCP protocol. The windowing feature identifies the amount of data that can be transferred before expecting an acknowledgment from the receiver.
Layer 3Network layerThis layer is responsible for data transfer between the networks with the help of logical addressing, such as IP addresses. L4 breaks down the data into smaller chunks, called data packets, before passing it on to L3.
表 6-1. OSI 模型：第 7 层应用层直接访问用户数据，软件应用通过 HTTP、SMTP、SSH 等协议依赖它；第 6 层表示层负责数据的格式化、加密/解密和压缩；第 5 层会话层负责会话的建立、维护和终止；第 4 层传输层通过 TCP、UDP 等协议在设备间传输数据，负责缓冲、差错控制和滑动窗口；第 3 层网络层借助 IP 地址等逻辑地址在网络间传输数据，L4 把数据拆成数据包后交给 L3。

Layer numberLayer nameLayer function
Layer 2Data link layerThis layer transfers data between devices, from the incoming network interface to the outgoing network interface, in the form of frames (packets are further broken down into data frames). This layer has two parts:
  • Medium access control (MAC) helps with the physical addressing of devices involved in network communication. The MAC address of any device is globally unique and can identify the device for data delivery.
  • Logical link control (LLC) helps with flow control and error control. The flow and error control in this layer is inside the same network as compared to L3, where it is across different networks.
Layer 1Physical layerThe data frames from L2 are converted to bit streams (in the form of ones and zeros) in L1. This layer involves the physical devices, such as cables and switches.
上表续：第 2 层数据链路层以帧的形式在设备之间传输数据（数据包进一步拆成数据帧），它分为两部分——MAC（介质访问控制）负责设备物理寻址，MAC 地址全局唯一；LLC（逻辑链路控制）负责流控和差错控制，且在同一网络内进行。第 1 层物理层把 L2 传来的数据帧转换为比特流（0 和 1），涉及电缆、交换机等物理设备。

In modern-age internet applications, we don't see an OSI model being practically present; it serves only as a reference communication model. In general, internet communications happen via the TCP/IP model. The TCP/IP model layers don't match one-to-one with the OSI model layers, but there are quite a few similarities.

在现代互联网应用中，我们看不到 OSI 模型被实际使用；它仅作为参考通信模型存在。一般来说，互联网通信通过 TCP/IP 模型进行。TCP/IP 模型的各层与 OSI 模型的各层并不是一一对应的，但有不少相似之处。

TCP/IP Model

The TCP/IP model, also referred to as the internet protocol suite, mainly includes TCP, IP, and UDP. The TCP/IP model combines multiple layers of the OSI model into one layer to execute similar functionality; the layers in the two models are compared in Table 6-2.

TCP/IP 模型，也称为互联网协议族，主要包括 TCP、IP 和 UDP。TCP/IP 模型把 OSI 模型的多层合并为一层来执行相似功能；两个模型的各层对比见表 6-2。

Table 6-2. Different layers of the OSI and TCP/IP models
OSI model layerTCP/IP model layerTCP/IP protocol examples
Application, presentation, sessionApplicationSMTP, HTTP
TransportTransportTCP, UDP
NetworkInternetIP, ICMP
Data linkData linkIEEE 802.2
PhysicalPhysical networkEthernet
表 6-2. OSI 与 TCP/IP 模型各层对照：OSI 的应用/表示/会话三层合并为 TCP/IP 的应用层（协议示例 SMTP、HTTP）；传输层对应传输层（TCP、UDP）；网络层对应互联网层（IP、ICMP）；数据链路层对应数据链路层（IEEE 802.2）；物理层对应物理网络层（以太网）。

Different protocols operate at different layers in the communication models. We'll discuss the more general ones to help you gain an understanding of how communication over the internet works, starting with the network layer protocols

不同协议运行在通信模型的不同层上。我们将讨论更通用的一些，帮助你理解互联网上的通信是如何工作的，从网络层协议开始

Page 161

such as IP, and we'll learn how different protocols are used for specific communication purposes.

（例如 IP）讲起，并了解不同协议如何用于特定通信目的。

Network layer protocols

The most used protocol in the network/internet layer is the Internet Protocol (IP). It is a set of rules responsible for delivering data packets from a source IP address to a destination IP address. (We'll discuss IP addresses and their types more in Chapter 9.) The IP address uniquely identifies the source and destination of data packets across the network and helps routers to route this information from one place to another.

网络/互联网层中最常用的协议是网际协议（IP）。它是一组规则，负责把数据包从源 IP 地址投递到目的 IP 地址。（我们将在第 9 章更多地讨论 IP 地址及其类型。）IP 地址在网络中唯一标识数据包的源和目的，并帮助路由器把这些信息从一个地方路由到另一个地方。

Data across the internet is often broken into chunks (referred to as fragmentation) to avoid the burden of delivering large packets and to reduce latency. There is also a limit to the maximum size of a packet (1,500 bytes for ethernet) that can be transmitted over the network interface: the maximum transmission unit (MTU).

互联网上的数据常被拆成块（称为分片），以避免投递大数据包的负担并降低延迟。网络接口上能传输的数据包最大大小也有限制（以太网为 1500 字节）：即最大传输单元（MTU）。

Each packet in IP protocol contains an IP header and payload. The IP header has the source IP address and the destination IP address, along with any other metadata (such as IP version, packet size, and TTL) required to route the packet. The payload consists of actual data (called IP datagrams) that is to be transferred over the network.

IP 协议中的每个数据包都包含一个 IP 头和载荷。IP 头有源 IP 地址和目的 IP 地址，以及路由该数据包所需的其他元数据（例如 IP 版本、包大小和 TTL）。载荷由要在网络上传输的实际数据（称为 IP 数据报）组成。

Another protocol that operates on this layer is the Internet Control Message Protocol (ICMP). This protocol is generally used for network diagnostics and implementing error mechanisms. For example, to check if Google servers are responding to traffic, we can use the command ping google.com (the command output is included here as reference). Let's say the google.com URL is not resolved to a server; the router can respond with an ICMP message to the sender:

在这一层运行的另一个协议是互联网控制报文协议（ICMP）。该协议通常用于网络诊断和实现差错机制。例如，要检查 Google 服务器是否响应流量，我们可以使用命令 ping google.com（命令输出附此供参考）。假设 google.com 这个 URL 没有解析到某台服务器，路由器可以用一条 ICMP 消息响应发送方：

PING google.com (142.250.74.206) 56(84) bytes of data.
64 bytes from fra24s02-in-f14.1e100.net (142.250.74.206): icmp_seq=1 ttl=116
64 bytes from fra24s02-in-f14.1e100.net (142.250.74.206): icmp_seq=2 ttl=116
64 bytes from fra24s02-in-f14.1e100.net (142.250.74.206): icmp_seq=3 ttl=116

The network layer protocols in general work in conjunction with transport layer protocols, such as TCP and UDP, for data delivery.

网络层协议通常与传输层协议（例如 TCP 和 UDP）协同工作来完成数据投递。

Transmission Control Protocol

The Transmission Control Protocol (TCP) is a transport layer protocol that offers reliable communication between sender and receiver with the capability of retransmitting data in case of packet loss. Communication via TCP is initiated between the sender and receiver via a three-way handshake process shown in Figure 6-1. The three-way handshake process is an agreement between the two parties to send and accept the data. The TCP header includes information like the source and destination port numbers, sequence number (identifies how much data is sent during a session), acknowledgment number (used at the receiver end to send an acknowledgment and a

传输控制协议（TCP）是一种传输层协议，它在发送方与接收方之间提供可靠通信，并能在丢包时重传数据。TCP 通信通过图 6-1 所示的三次握手过程在发送方与接收方之间发起。三次握手过程是双方就发送和接收数据达成的一致。TCP 头包含源端口号和目的端口号、序列号（标识一次会话中发送了多少数据）、确认号（在接收端用于发送确认和

Page 162

request for the next segment), and window (the number of bytes a receiver can accept from a sender).

对下一个报文段的请求）以及窗口（接收方能从发送方接受的字节数）等信息。

Once the connection is established after a successful handshake, the protocol needs to figure out the optimal amount of data (window size) that can be transmitted before waiting for an acknowledgment (ACK), ensuring available bandwidth utilization and data transfer without network congestion. This is achieved by two mechanisms: slow start and congestion avoidance.

握手成功、连接建立后，协议需要算出在等待确认（ACK）之前可以传输的最优数据量（窗口大小），以确保可用带宽被利用、且数据传输不会造成网络拥塞。这通过两种机制实现：慢启动和拥塞避免。

The data transfer begins with a small data size (one segment in a congestion window)—hence the term slow start—and the sender gradually increases the window size in an exponential manner (the window is increased by one segment on every ACK). The maximum allowed data transfer size depends on the advertised window size by the receiver. If the allowed internet bandwidth is surpassed, the intermediate router (or the receiver) discards the data packets. Congestion is detected if there are connection timeouts or if duplicate ACKs are received. Congestion avoidance kicks in to deal with these dropped packets, and the congestion window size is halved and set to one segment for timeout scenarios.

数据传输以较小的数据量开始（拥塞窗口中的一个报文段）——因此称为慢启动——发送方以指数方式逐渐增大窗口大小（每收到一个 ACK，窗口增加一个报文段）。允许的最大数据传输量取决于接收方通告的窗口大小。如果超过了可用的互联网带宽，中间路由器（或接收方）就会丢弃数据包。如果出现连接超时或收到重复 ACK，就检测到了拥塞。拥塞避免开始处理这些被丢弃的包，拥塞窗口大小减半；在超时场景下则设为一个报文段。

We recommend deploying applications in closer vicinity (the same geographic region) to improve performance. Closeness reduces the number of network hops and improves the round trip time (RTT), helping the sender quickly adjust the congestion window size for any congestion occurrence.

我们建议把应用部署在更近的位置（同一地理区域）以提升性能。位置近减少了网络跳数并改善了往返时间（RTT），帮助发送方在发生拥塞时快速调整拥塞窗口大小。

Page 163

A connection has both a source and a destination port for communication. A port is a virtual point managed by an OS that defines an entry to or exit from a software application (numbered from 0 to 65535). You can compare them to your personal computer ports, such as USB ports. Each port is responsible for certain types of network communication, and the role is assigned based on the range it falls into. The following are the three divisions of range from 0 to 65535:

一条通信连接同时有一个源端口和一个目的端口。端口是由操作系统管理的虚拟点，定义了进入或离开某个软件应用的出入口（编号从 0 到 65535）。你可以把它们类比为个人电脑上的 USB 端口。每个端口负责特定类型的网络通信，其角色根据它所属的范围来分配。0 到 65535 分为以下三个区间：

  • Well-known ports. Ports with numbers from 0 to 1023 are called well-known ports (also known as system ports). These ports are used by system processes and controlled by the Internet Assigned Numbers Authority (IANA). For example, Port 22 is used for Secure Shell (SSH), and Port 80 is used for HTTP.
    知名端口。编号 0 到 1023 的端口称为知名端口（也叫系统端口）。这些端口由系统进程使用，由互联网号码分配机构（IANA）控制。例如，22 端口用于安全 Shell（SSH），80 端口用于 HTTP。
  • Registered ports. Ports with numbers from 1024 to 49151 are called registered ports (also known as user ports). These ports are used by user processes. For example, Port 1194 is used for OpenVPN. Both well-known and registered ports are also referred to as nonephemeral ports and are assigned by IANA.
    注册端口。编号 1024 到 49151 的端口称为注册端口（也叫用户端口）。这些端口由用户进程使用。例如，1194 端口用于 OpenVPN。知名端口和注册端口也统称为非临时端口，由 IANA 分配。
  • Ephemeral ports. Ports with numbers from 49152 to 65535 are called ephemeral ports (also known as private or dynamic ports). These ports are not controlled by IANA and can be used for private or temporary purposes.
    临时端口。编号 49152 到 65535 的端口称为临时端口（也叫私有或动态端口）。这些端口不受 IANA 控制，可用于私有或临时用途。

We described the additional work, such as establishing communication or retransmitting lost packets with TCP, that comes with the extra cost of latency. If there are no such requirements, we can go with another transport layer protocol: User Datagram Protocol (UDP).

我们描述了 TCP 建立通信或重传丢包所做的额外工作，这些都会带来额外的延迟代价。如果没有这类需求，我们可以选用另一种传输层协议：用户数据报协议（UDP）。

User Datagram Protocol

Some business use cases where latency (real-time communication) is more important than dropping packets include voice and video calls, live event streaming, gaming, and DNS. The UDP transport protocol is less reliable but faster than TCP and works for these use cases. It is faster because it doesn't involve a three-way handshake process for establishing a connection, and it provides no guarantee of data delivery, so there is no overhead of retries.

有些业务用例中，延迟（实时通信）比丢包更重要，例如语音和视频通话、现场活动直播、游戏和 DNS。UDP 传输协议不如 TCP 可靠，但比 TCP 快，适合这些用例。它更快是因为它不需要三次握手来建立连接，也不保证数据投递，因此没有重试开销。

The UDP header includes information like the source and destination ports, length, UDP checksum, and data. The UDP header is not as heavy as the TCP header as it holds the minimum data for segment delivery and doesn't provide assurance of the order of segments (data received at the receiver might not be in the same order as sent by the sender). However, not having a three-way handshake between the sender and receiver to start communication can present a security threat. To illustrate how this works, let's first discuss the steps in communicating via UDP:

UDP 头包含源端口、目的端口、长度、UDP 校验和以及数据等信息。UDP 头不像 TCP 头那么重，因为它只携带报文段投递所需的最少数据，也不保证报文段的顺序（接收方收到的数据可能与发送方发送的顺序不同）。然而，发送方与接收方之间没有三次握手就开始通信，可能带来安全威胁。为说明它如何工作，我们先讨论通过 UDP 通信的步骤：

Page 164
  1. A sender sends a UDP segment to a destination on a specific port.
    发送方把一个 UDP 报文段发送到特定端口上的某个目的地。
  2. The receiver checks if the request is expected by any application on that port. If yes, then the request is consumed by the application for further processing.
    接收方检查该端口上是否有某个应用期望接收此请求。如果有，该请求就被应用消费以做进一步处理。
  3. If no, the receiver responds with an ICMP packet mentioning that the destination is not reachable.
    如果没有，接收方就用一个 ICMP 包响应，告知目的地不可达。

Given that this processing happens at a large scale, some bad actors can intentionally bombard UDP requests to the server so that server resources are entirely consumed in responding to the requests, causing denial of service to actual traffic. We need to add mechanisms to our systems to mitigate these kinds of issues. One way could be to ignore these requests after a configured threshold by not responding with ICMP messages. The downside of this approach is potentially dropping actual customer requests, but at least we'll be able to keep our system healthy. Another way could be to leverage third-party applications offered by cloud providers, such as AWS Shield.

由于这种处理是大规模进行的，一些恶意者可以故意向服务器大量发送 UDP 请求，使服务器资源完全消耗在响应这些请求上，从而对真实流量造成拒绝服务。我们需要在系统中加入机制来缓解这类问题。一种方式是在达到配置阈值后忽略这些请求，不再用 ICMP 消息响应。这种方式的缺点是可能丢弃真实的客户请求，但至少能保持系统健康。另一种方式是利用云提供商提供的第三方应用，例如 AWS Shield。

Both TCP and UDP serve their purposes, and you should choose based on your business requirements. We prefer TCP for reliability and full-duplex (bidirectional) communications, and UDP for faster response times and unidirectional communications.

TCP 和 UDP 各有其用途，你应根据业务需求选择。我们在需要可靠性和全双工（双向）通信时偏好 TCP，在需要更快响应时间和单向通信时偏好 UDP。

The layer operating on top of the network layer is the application layer in the TCP/IP model. Let's dig deeper into a few application layer protocols, starting with HTTP.

在网络层之上运行的是 TCP/IP 模型中的应用层。下面我们深入了解几种应用层协议，从 HTTP 开始。

Hypertext Transfer Protocol

The world heavily depends on the internet for day-to-day work, and most of this work happens in web browsers and software applications running on mobile devices. Communications over the internet generally follow the client-server model, where a client requests some information (an HTTP request) and the server responds with data (an HTTP response) corresponding to the request on port 80 (port 443 for HTTPS, a secure version of HTTP). To gain more familiarity with how the protocol works, take a look at an example HTTP request for retrieving customer orders based on order ID:

世界的日常工作高度依赖互联网，而这些工作大多发生在网页浏览器和运行在移动设备上的软件应用中。互联网上的通信通常遵循客户端-服务器模型：客户端请求某些信息（HTTP 请求），服务器在 80 端口（HTTPS 则用 443 端口，HTTPS 是 HTTP 的安全版本）上返回与请求对应的数据（HTTP 响应）。为了更熟悉该协议的工作方式，请看一个根据订单 ID 检索客户订单的 HTTP 请求示例：

GET /api/orders?id=23234555&customerId=dhfsd348e48ddd HTTP/1.1
Host: api.myFoodApp.com
Authorization: Bearer MyAccessToken
User-Agent: MyOnlineFoodOrderApplication/1.0
Accept: application/json

HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Content-Type: application/json
{
  "orderId": "23234555",
  "customerId": "dhfsd348e48ddd",
  "amount": 199,
  "currency": "INR",
  "items": [

    {
      "product": "Paneer Tikka Masala",

      "product": "Tandoori Roti Butter",

The request responses included in this chapter are for illustrative purposes only and were not tested in the production environment.
本章中包含的请求/响应仅作演示用途，未在生产环境中测试。

The HTTP request contains details like the HTTP method (GET in this case), version (1.1), and host specifying where the request is being routed to with the required authentication mechanism. We can specify different HTTP methods (GET, HEAD, POST, PUT, DELETE, CONNECT, OPTIONS, TRACE, PATCH) based on the type of call to the server. The following are the most widely used methods:

HTTP 请求包含 HTTP 方法（本例中为 GET）、版本（1.1）以及 host（指定请求路由到哪里，并带上所需的认证机制）等细节。根据对服务器调用的类型，我们可以指定不同的 HTTP 方法（GET、HEAD、POST、PUT、DELETE、CONNECT、OPTIONS、TRACE、PATCH）。以下是最广泛使用的方法：

  • GET method. Used to retrieve data without any state modification inside the system (ensures idempotent nature). For example, retrieve order details based on order ID and customer ID.
    GET 方法。用于检索数据，而不对系统内部做任何状态修改（保证幂等性）。例如，根据订单 ID 和客户 ID 检索订单详情。
  • POST method. Used to create a new resource on the server or send any data for processing and is nonidempotent in nature. For example, place a food order and complete the transaction.
    POST 方法。用于在服务器上创建新资源或发送待处理的数据，本质上是非幂等的。例如，下一个餐饮订单并完成交易。
  • PUT method. Used to update any resource on the server and is idempotent in nature. For example, update the address after placing an order.
    PUT 方法。用于更新服务器上的某个资源，本质上是幂等的。例如，下单后更新地址。
  • DELETE method. Used to remove any resource from the server and is idempotent in nature. For example, delete a saved address entry.
    DELETE 方法。用于从服务器上移除某个资源，本质上是幂等的。例如，删除一个已保存的地址条目。
Page 166
The POST, PUT, and DELETE method APIs should be idempotent in nature, but the actual nature of the APIs still depends on the developer's code. Follow the general guidelines of idempotent nature based on method type to avoid unintended system behavior.
POST、PUT、DELETE 方法的 API 本质上应是幂等的，但 API 的实际行为仍取决于开发者的代码。请遵循基于方法类型的幂等性通用准则，以避免非预期的系统行为。

Next to the HTTP method is the request target specifying the location on the host (server) that the client is trying to access. HTTP has evolved, and the version represents which particular specification the application is using. Older versions are deprecated. The most used versions these days are:

HTTP 方法之后是请求目标，指定客户端试图访问主机（服务器）上的哪个位置。HTTP 已经演进，版本表示应用正在使用哪份规范。较老的版本已废弃。如今最常用的版本有：

  • HTTP/1.1. The most widely used version, HTTP/1.1 offers better support to previous versions, such as reuse of TCP connections to make multiple requests.
    HTTP/1.1。最广泛使用的版本，HTTP/1.1 对先前版本提供了更好的支持，例如复用 TCP 连接来发起多个请求。
  • HTTP/2. HTTP/2 optimizes the header to be available in a compressed format (less bandwidth compared to HTTP/1.1), with a single TCP connection for a domain and server push capability to avoid any polling from clients for asynchronous calls (we will elaborate on this in upcoming sections).
    HTTP/2。HTTP/2 把头优化为压缩格式可用（相比 HTTP/1.1 带宽更少），一个域名使用单条 TCP 连接，并具备服务器推送能力，以避免客户端为异步调用做轮询（我们将在后续章节详述）。
  • HTTP/3. HTTP/3 improves speed (compared to HTTP/2) by using UDP instead of TCP/IP protocols, also referred to as QUIC (Quick UDP Internet Connections). Therefore, it avoids occasional TCP/IP congestion problems by implementing a congestion control algorithm.
    HTTP/3。HTTP/3 通过使用 UDP 而非 TCP/IP 协议来提升速度（相比 HTTP/2），也称为 QUIC（快速 UDP 互联网连接）。因此，它通过实现拥塞控制算法避免了偶发的 TCP/IP 拥塞问题。

There can be some additional metadata as part of the request, referred to as the HTTP header. It can include information like the user agent (where the request is being made from, such as a software application or web browser name), accept (the type of content format expected from the server), and so on.

请求中还可以包含一些额外元数据，称为 HTTP 头。它可以包括 user agent（请求从哪里发出，例如软件应用或网页浏览器名称）、accept（期望从服务器返回的内容格式类型）等信息。

The HTTP response includes the response to the request (order details for order ID and customer ID). Alongside the response object, it has the HTTP status code. The status code represents what happened with the request. For example, "200 OK" means the request was successfully processed by the server. The status codes range from the 100 series to the 500 series and are listed in Table 6-3.

HTTP 响应包含对请求的响应（对应订单 ID 和客户 ID 的订单详情）。除了响应对象外，它还有 HTTP 状态码。状态码表示请求发生了什么。例如，“200 OK”表示请求被服务器成功处理。状态码从 100 系列到 500 系列，列于表 6-3。

Table 6-3. HTTP response status codes
Status code seriesStatus code meaning and examples
100For informational purposes, such as noting that the server has received the request and it is in processing.
  • 100: Continue
  • 101: Switching protocols
表 6-3. HTTP 响应状态码：100 系列为信息性状态，表示服务器已收到请求正在处理（100 Continue、101 Switching Protocols）。

Status code seriesStatus code meaning and examples
200Notes that the request has been successfully processed by the server.
  • 200: OK with the response associated with the corresponding request
  • 201: The request has been processed by the server, and a new resource has been created.
300The server has redirected the request to another resource for fulfilling it.
  • 301: The resource has moved permanently to a new location, and the client should update the references on its end. The location header in the response contains the updated URL reference.
  • 302: The resource has temporarily moved to a new location.
400There was an issue in the client request that should be rectified before sending it to the server.
  • 400: The request is not as expected for the server request target.
  • 401: The request doesn't contain valid credentials for authentication.
  • 403: The client is not authorized for the request.
  • 404: The requested resource is not available on the server.
500The server encountered an error while the request was being processed.
  • 500: The server encountered some unexpected exception while processing the request.
  • 503: The server is temporarily unavailable to take client requests.
上表续：200 系列表示请求被服务器成功处理（200 OK、201 Created）；300 系列表示服务器把请求重定向到另一资源（301 永久移动、302 临时移动）；400 系列表示客户端请求有问题，需修正后再发（400 错误请求、401 未认证、403 禁止访问、404 未找到）；500 系列表示服务器处理请求时出错（500 内部错误、503 暂时不可用）。

HTTP is a general protocol for application communications over the internet. Some protocols are designed to solve specific use cases, such as Simple Mail Transfer Protocol (SMTP) for email communications.

HTTP 是互联网上应用通信的通用协议。有些协议是为解决特定用例而设计的，例如用于电子邮件通信的简单邮件传输协议（SMTP）。

Simple Mail Transfer Protocol

Email access was directly tied to personal computers in the early days, and an email software application needed to be installed on the computer to download emails for reading. The limitations of this approach included having to own a personal computer (not so common in the early days of the internet), setting up email clients (which could be complex), and synchronizing across the devices. The solution was a web-based email client launched by Hotmail as a free service in 1996.

早期，电子邮件的访问直接绑定到个人电脑上，需要在电脑上安装邮件软件应用才能下载邮件阅读。这种方式的局限包括：必须拥有一台个人电脑（在互联网早期并不常见）、要设置邮件客户端（可能很复杂）、以及跨设备同步。解决方案是 Hotmail 于 1996 年作为免费服务推出的基于 Web 的邮件客户端。

The software applications interact via application layer protocols like SMTP for email services and forward the communication flow through other layers in the TCP/IP model. The SMTP protocol is used for email communications between two or more parties. Let's look at an example (shown in Figure 6-2) of how a person can send an email via different mail agents.

软件应用通过 SMTP 等应用层协议为邮件服务交互，并把通信流经 TCP/IP 模型的其他层转发。SMTP 协议用于两个或多个参与方之间的电子邮件通信。下面我们看一个例子（图 6-2），了解一个人如何通过不同的邮件代理发送电子邮件。

The SMTP client identifies the mail domain (such as gmail.com, hotmail.com, etc.) and then establishes a two-way stateful transmission channel to the corresponding SMTP server(s) to transfer mail. The connection is initiated via SMTP commands, and the server replies to corresponding commands with success or failure. The SMTP server can be the destination of mail delivery, or it can be an intermediate server to forward the mail. When the sender and receiver belong to different domains (for

SMTP 客户端识别邮件域名（例如 gmail.com、hotmail.com 等），然后与相应的 SMTP 服务器建立一条双向有状态的传输通道来传输邮件。连接通过 SMTP 命令发起，服务器对相应命令回复成功或失败。SMTP 服务器可以是邮件投递的目的地，也可以是转发邮件的中间服务器。当发送方和接收方属于不同域名（例如

Page 168

example, email from gmail.com to hotmail.com), the intermediate server is called a relay server.

从 gmail.com 发到 hotmail.com 的邮件）时，中间服务器称为中继服务器（relay server）。

Let's compare this to physical mail delivery: you've gone to the local post office and mailed two letters—one to be delivered in your own town and another to be delivered to a friend in a nearby town. The first letter can be delivered without involving any other post office, but in the case of the second, the letter is transferred to the post office of the nearby town and then delivered to your friend. Because our delivery agents can't directly go to other towns to deliver letters, we require another post office in between—the relay server, in the case of SMTP—to bear this responsibility.

我们把它和实物邮件投递做个类比：你去当地邮局寄了两封信——一封在你自己镇上投递，另一封寄给附近镇上的朋友。第一封信不需要其他邮局参与就能投递；但第二封信需要转到附近镇上的邮局，然后再投递给你的朋友。因为我们的投递员不能直接去别的镇上送信，我们就需要中间有另一个邮局——在 SMTP 中就是中继服务器——来承担这个责任。

The SMTP server can also behave as a gateway, meaning that further transport of mail is carried out with the help of other protocols, not via SMTP. SMTP clients and servers are also referred to as mail transfer agents (MTAs) because they offer the mail transfer service. SMTP commands are used for communication between the parties, and replies include a success or failure acknowledgment corresponding to the commands sent.

SMTP 服务器也可以充当网关，即邮件的进一步传输借助其他协议完成，而不是通过 SMTP。SMTP 客户端和服务器也称为邮件传输代理（MTA），因为它们提供邮件传输服务。SMTP 命令用于各参与方之间的通信，回复包含与所发命令对应的成功或失败确认。

We often add media to emails as attachments, which are not inherently supported by SMTP. For these purposes, we use Multipurpose Internet Mail Extensions (MIMEs). The MIME protocol makes SMTP extensible to support media attachments and conversion of non-ASCII characters to 7-bit ASCII characters (English language alphabets and numbers). Recall that we described ports very briefly when discussing TCP—SMTP operates on Port 25 for plain-text communications and Port 587 for encrypted mail communications.

我们常在邮件中以附件形式添加媒体，而 SMTP 本身并不支持附件。为此，我们使用多用途互联网邮件扩展（MIME）。MIME 协议让 SMTP 可扩展，以支持媒体附件以及把非 ASCII 字符转换为 7 位 ASCII 字符（英文字母和数字）。回忆一下我们在讨论 TCP 时简略提到的端口——SMTP 在 25 端口上进行明文通信，在 587 端口上进行加密邮件通信。

SMTP essentially operates on a push mechanism, transferring email contents from clients to servers. There are two other protocols, Post Office Protocol (POP) and Internet Message Access Protocol (IMAP), that specifically work on the pull mechanism, retrieving the email from servers to send to user devices. POP connects with the email servers, downloads the content to the local machine, and deletes the emails from the server. IMAP directly reads from servers without downloading content to the local machine or deleting the emails after reading. Both these protocols have their benefits. POP is fast because the message is predownloaded for reading, but since

SMTP 本质上运行在推送机制上，把邮件内容从客户端传输到服务器。还有另外两种协议——邮局协议（POP）和互联网消息访问协议（IMAP）——专门运行在拉取机制上，把邮件从服务器取回并发送到用户设备。POP 连接邮件服务器，把内容下载到本地机器，然后从服务器删除邮件。IMAP 直接从服务器读取，而不把内容下载到本地机器，也不在读取后删除邮件。这两种协议各有优势。POP 很快，因为消息被预下载下来供阅读，但由于

Page 169

the messages are deleted from the servers, we can't read the same emails on different devices. IMAP allows us to read emails on any number of devices, but it is not as fast as POP.

消息从服务器上被删除，我们就不能在不同设备上阅读同一批邮件。IMAP 允许我们在任意数量的设备上阅读邮件，但它不如 POP 快。

We've discussed protocols designed specifically for email communications, but email communications are not near real time. Next, we'll move to the Extensible Messaging and Presence Protocol (XMPP), which offers near real-time communication over the internet.

我们讨论了专为电子邮件通信设计的协议，但电子邮件通信并不是近实时的。接下来，我们转向可扩展消息与呈现协议（XMPP），它在互联网上提供近实时通信。

Extensible Messaging and Presence Protocol

XMPP is an instant message protocol based on Extensible Markup Language (XML) with additional features, such as presence information (noting when a user is online or offline) and a contact list (called a roster). XMPP helps keep communication near real time among users by streaming XML stanzas (a fundamental unit of communication in XMPP with message and recipient information) over a persistent TCP or HTTP connection. XMPP can be operated in a more efficient manner using WebSockets as a subprotocol (we'll discuss this shortly) instead of HTTP binding since WebSockets are inherently built for bidirectional communications. This protocol can operate in asynchronous fashion as well, which essentially means the recipient user doesn't have to be online. This can be helpful in use cases like notification broadcasting.

XMPP 是一种基于可扩展标记语言（XML）的即时消息协议，带有呈现信息（标注用户何时在线或离线）和联系人列表（称为 roster）等附加特性。XMPP 通过在持久的 TCP 或 HTTP 连接上流式传输 XML stanza（XMPP 中承载消息和接收方信息的基本通信单元），帮助用户之间保持近实时通信。由于 WebSocket 天生就是为双向通信构建的，XMPP 可以使用 WebSocket 作为子协议（我们稍后讨论）而非 HTTP 绑定来更高效地运行。该协议也可以异步运行，本质上意味着接收方用户不必在线。这在通知广播等用例中很有用。

The lifecycle of an XMPP connection starts with the client initiating a TCP connection with a server on Port 5222 for plain text and 5223 for encrypted communications. The next steps are:

XMPP 连接的生命周期始于客户端与服务器建立 TCP 连接：明文用 5222 端口，加密通信用 5223 端口。接下来的步骤是：

  1. The client sends a stream header to start the negotiation process for stream features, such as authentication mechanisms and encryption methods.
    客户端发送流头，开始协商流特性的过程，例如认证机制和加密方法。
  2. After negotiation, the client shares credentials for authentication depending on whether that was agreed to during the negotiation process.
    协商完成后，客户端根据协商过程中是否就此达成一致，分享用于认证的凭据。
  3. The client binds to a resource. This enables unique identification with the use of a Jabber ID, which we'll explain shortly.
    客户端绑定到一个资源。这使得可以使用 Jabber ID 进行唯一标识，我们稍后解释。
  4. The client can establish a session (if needed) by sending a session request to a server.
    客户端可以通过向服务器发送会话请求来建立会话（如果需要）。
  5. Once a session is established, the client shares the presence information with the server. Now the client can request a roster and continue with sending or receiving messages via XML stanzas.
    会话建立后，客户端与服务器分享呈现信息。现在客户端可以请求 roster，并继续通过 XML stanza 发送或接收消息。
  6. As with any other protocol, the connection is terminated at the end of the session once requested by the client and acknowledged by the server.
    与任何其他协议一样，在会话结束时，经客户端请求并由服务器确认后，连接被终止。

XMPP is a decentralized protocol—meaning anyone can host XMPP servers—and works like SMTP. Every user has a unique ID referred to as a Jabber ID (JID—note

XMPP 是一种去中心化协议——意味着任何人都可以托管 XMPP 服务器——其工作方式类似 SMTP。每个用户都有一个唯一 ID，称为 Jabber ID（JID——注意

Page 170

that XMPP was previously known as Jabber), which is like an email address. The JID is denoted by a unique user ID along with the domain name (e.g., myUserId@example.com). The user may log in from multiple devices, which can be represented by specifying the resource identifier, such as myUserId@example.com/mobile.

XMPP 以前称为 Jabber），它就像一个电子邮件地址。JID 由一个唯一用户 ID 加上域名表示（例如 myUserId@example.com）。用户可能从多台设备登录，这可以通过指定资源标识符来表示，例如 myUserId@example.com/mobile。

XMPP is a widely used protocol for chat applications; for example, you may have used or heard about the WhatsApp chat application. WhatsApp is built on top of ejabberd, an open source software application written in the Erlang programming language that operates over XMPP.

XMPP 是聊天应用广泛使用的协议；例如，你可能用过或听说过 WhatsApp 聊天应用。WhatsApp 构建在 ejabberd 之上，ejabberd 是一个用 Erlang 编程语言编写、运行在 XMPP 之上的开源软件应用。

Message Queuing Telemetry Transport (MQTT) is another real-time protocol that we'll discuss next.

消息队列遥测传输（MQTT）是我们接下来要讨论的另一种实时协议。

Message Queuing Telemetry Transport

As its name suggests, MQTT was originally designed for applications to send telemetry data to and from space probes using minimum resources. The MQTT protocol is heavily used for IoT device communication and can support messaging applications as well. MQTT is based on the pub/sub model: users send messages to a topic (publish) and receive them by subscribing to topics. The publishers and subscribers are completely independent of one another, and the pub/sub actions are facilitated by MQTT brokers, as shown in Figure 6-3.

顾名思义，MQTT 最初是为应用与太空探测器之间用最少资源收发遥测数据而设计的。MQTT 协议大量用于 IoT 设备通信，也能支持消息应用。MQTT 基于发布/订阅（pub/sub）模型：用户把消息发到某个主题（发布），并通过订阅主题来接收消息。发布者和订阅者彼此完全独立，发布/订阅动作由 MQTT broker 促成，如图 6-3 所示。

MQTT supports bidirectional communications between the devices and the cloud and offers multiple quality of service (QoS) levels for ensuring message delivery guarantees. The QoS levels are defined separately by the publisher (to publish a message to a topic) and the subscriber (to consume a message from a topic). The three QoS levels supported by MQTT are:

MQTT 支持设备与云之间的双向通信，并提供多个服务质量（QoS）级别来保证消息投递。QoS 级别由发布者（向主题发布消息）和订阅者（从主题消费消息）分别定义。MQTT 支持的三个 QoS 级别是：

  • At most once—QoS Level 0. QoS 0 is based on the principle of "fire and forget." The sender publishes a message only once (no retransmission), and the consumer doesn't acknowledge receiving a message for confirmation. QoS Level 0 is simplest to implement as no guarantees need to be ensured for message delivery.
    至多一次——QoS 0。QoS 0 基于“发后即忘”原则。发送方只发布一次消息（不重传），消费方也不对收到消息做确认。QoS 0 实现最简单，因为不需要保证消息投递。
  • At least once—QoS Level 1. QoS 1 ensures the message is delivered to the subscriber at least once, so there is a possibility of duplicate messages, and the subscriber should appropriately handle that. The publisher waits for an acknowledgment of message delivery and
    至少一次——QoS 1。QoS 1 确保消息至少被投递到订阅者一次，因此可能出现重复消息，订阅者应妥善处理。发布者等待消息投递的确认，
Page 171
  • retransmits the message if the acknowledgment is not received within a certain time frame. This level is intermediary between Level 0 and Level 1 in terms of both reliability and implementation.
    如果在一定时间内未收到确认就重传消息。这个级别在可靠性和实现复杂度上都介于 0 级和 1 级之间。
  • Exactly once—QoS Level 2. QoS 2 guarantees "exactly once" message delivery to the recipients. This is achieved by four-part verification between the publisher and subscriber for every message (thus reducing efficiency and complicating the implementation).
    恰好一次——QoS 2。QoS 2 保证消息“恰好一次”投递到接收方。这通过发布者与订阅者之间对每条消息的四次交互校验来实现（因此降低了效率并使实现复杂化）。

We can select the QoS levels based on the efficiency and reliability requirements. QoS 0 is most efficient but least reliable, while QoS 2 is most reliable but least efficient.

我们可以根据效率和可靠性需求选择 QoS 级别。QoS 0 最高效但最不可靠，而 QoS 2 最可靠但最低效。

Protocols are essentially a set of rules to establish communication among the involved parties. In the next section, we'll discuss the different communication types available over the internet and how we can use them as necessary for our business needs.

协议本质上是一套规则，用于在各参与方之间建立通信。在下一节中，我们将讨论互联网上可用的不同通信类型，以及如何根据业务需要使用它们。

Communication Types

We briefly touched on the general idea of synchronous (sync) and asynchronous (async) communication in Chapter 1. In synchronous communication between two parties, the first party requests some data and then waits for the response from the second party. In the case of asynchronous communication, the first party requests some data but doesn't wait for the response. The second party can respond in the near future via events or any other mechanism. Both the sync and the async modes of communications have their own sets of challenges and benefits, and it's very important that we identify when to use which for our business use cases.

我们在第 1 章简略提到了同步（sync）和异步（async）通信的大致概念。在两方之间的同步通信中，第一方请求某些数据，然后等待第二方的响应。在异步通信中，第一方请求某些数据但不等待响应。第二方可以在不久的将来通过事件或其他机制响应。同步和异步两种通信模式各有其挑战和好处，对于业务用例识别何时使用哪一种非常重要。

Sync communications are generally preferred for low-latency calls: we're aware that the server will return the response for the corresponding request within the expected time frame and won't take too long. The premise is that if we already know the request is going to take time to process, then we're blocking a system resource at the client's end and not performing any actual work. Note that using async mode doesn't mean the system is latency heavy—the request can be processed as soon as it is consumed by the service here as well. The fundamental difference lies in the method of communication.

同步通信通常更适合低延迟调用：我们知道服务器会在预期时间内返回对应请求的响应，不会太久。其前提是：如果我们已经知道请求需要时间处理，那我们就是在客户端一端阻塞了一个系统资源，却没有做任何实际工作。注意，使用异步模式并不意味着系统延迟重——请求在这里也可以在被服务消费后立即处理。根本区别在于通信方式。

With async calls, the response is not immediately returned for a request nor is it returned over the same connection. There are two ways to receive a response in the near future: either the client sends a request to the server again after some time, requesting a response, or the server delivers the response without the client needing to request it. The first mechanism is referred to as a pull-based mechanism, and the second is called a push-based mechanism.

对于异步调用，响应不会立即随请求返回，也不会在同一条连接上返回。在不久的将来接收响应有两种方式：要么客户端过一段时间再次向服务器发请求来索要响应，要么服务器无需客户端请求就直接把响应送达。第一种机制称为拉取式机制，第二种称为推送式机制。

Page 172

There can be multiple methods of communication in the pull- and push-based mechanisms. We'll discuss them one by one, beginning with the pull-based approaches—namely, HTTP regular polling and HTTP long polling.

拉取式和推送式机制中可以有多种通信方法。我们逐一讨论，从拉取式方法开始——即 HTTP 常规轮询和 HTTP 长轮询。

Pull Mechanism: HTTP Polling

Let's take an example of an online food-ordering platform to understand the different kinds of pull mechanisms. Once an order is placed, we want to know its status, such as order preparation is ongoing, a delivery agent is assigned, the delivery agent has picked up the food, the delivery agent is at a particular location, and finally, food is delivered at our doorstep. Table 6-4 lists different approaches that the client application can take to request the latest status of the order from the server application.

我们以一个在线订餐平台为例来理解不同种类的拉取机制。下单后，我们想知道它的状态，例如正在备餐、已分配配送员、配送员已取餐、配送员到达某个位置，最后餐品送到家门口。表 6-4 列出了客户端应用可以用来向服务器应用请求订单最新状态的不同方法。

Table 6-4. Pull-mechanism approaches
ApproachApproach considerations
HTTP regular polling: 1. Clients ask the server for a recent status at regular intervals, such as five seconds. 2. The server checks the status and responds back.Clients regularly invoke an API and might not get a response, wasting network bandwidth. We don't recommend this approach for production workloads as it will consume unnecessary resources.
HTTP long polling: 1. Clients ask the server for a recent status at regular intervals, such as one minute. 2. The server responds only if there is a change in status; otherwise, it holds the connection for a fixed interval, such as one minute. 3. The client reestablishes the connection after this interval to check for the most recent status.This requires fewer server calls compared to HTTP regular polling, reducing overall resource consumption; hence, the approach is an improvement over HTTP regular polling.
表 6-4. 拉取机制方法对比：HTTP 常规轮询是客户端每隔固定间隔（如 5 秒）向服务器询问最新状态，服务器检查后响应；缺点是客户端频繁调用 API 却可能拿不到新响应，浪费带宽，不建议生产环境使用。HTTP 长轮询是客户端每隔较长间隔（如 1 分钟）询问，服务器仅在状态变化时才响应，否则保持连接一段固定时间；客户端在该间隔后重新建立连接以检查最新状态。相比常规轮询，服务器调用更少、资源消耗更低，是一种改进。
Implement an exponential strategy in case a response is not received in the first call. For example, you might have seen how Gmail responds when there's no internet connection. First, it tries to connect within 1 second, then within 5 seconds, then 30 seconds, and so on.
如果第一次调用没有收到响应，应实现指数退避策略。例如，你可能见过 Gmail 在没有网络连接时如何响应：它先在 1 秒内尝试连接，然后 5 秒，再 30 秒，依此类推。

The next set of approaches that we're going to discuss are push-based mechanisms, which essentially means that clients don't ask for a response; it's the server's responsibility to send a response once the results are ready.

接下来要讨论的是推送式机制，本质上意味着客户端不索要响应；一旦结果就绪，由服务器负责把响应发送出去。

Push Mechanism: WebSockets

In HTTP long polling, the connection is terminated after a certain time, and then the client reinitiates a connection. But what if we require a persistent connection? WebSockets represent a bidirectional persistent connection (full-duplex communication on a single TCP connection) over HTTP where clients and servers communicate with each other. Once the connection is established between the client and server, the messages can flow to and fro. A popular example for these kinds of requirements is a chat application (architecture details are given in Chapter 19). Two people (or more, in the case of user groups) interact with each other in real time, so a persistent

在 HTTP 长轮询中，连接在一段时间后终止，然后客户端重新发起连接。但如果我们需要一条持久连接呢？WebSocket 表示在 HTTP 之上的一条双向持久连接（单条 TCP 连接上的全双工通信），客户端和服务器通过它相互通信。一旦客户端与服务器之间的连接建立，消息就可以双向流动。这类需求的一个流行例子是聊天应用（架构细节见第 19 章）。两个人（或用户群情况下更多人）实时交互，因此持久

Page 173

connection makes more sense here compared to the client application asking for a response again and again.

连接比客户端应用反复索要响应更合理。

The WebSocket connection follows a similar flow as TCP. Any connection is started with a handshake process, and then the actual data transfer happens. The handshake process before data transfer ensures the agreement between the client and the server for bidirectional communication. The first step is that the client initiates an HTTP GET call (see the following code snippet) to the host server with the Connection type set as Upgrade and a Sec-WebSocket-Key (random base64-encoded key) for ensuring security:

WebSocket 连接遵循与 TCP 类似的流程。任何连接都以握手过程开始，然后才是实际的数据传输。数据传输前的握手过程确保客户端与服务器就双向通信达成一致。第一步是客户端向主机服务器发起一个 HTTP GET 调用（见以下代码片段），把 Connection 类型设为 Upgrade，并带上一个 Sec-WebSocket-Key（随机 base64 编码的密钥）以确保安全：

GET ws://myChatApp.com/chat HTTP/1.1
Host: myChatApp.com
Connection: Upgrade
Upgrade: websocket
Sec-WebSocket-Version: 13
Sec-WebSocket-Key: q4xkcO32u266gldTuKaSOw==

Once the server receives this request, it responds with HTTP status code 101, meaning the protocol is switched from HTTP to WebSocket. This is shown in the following code snippet:

服务器收到此请求后，以 HTTP 状态码 101 响应，表示协议从 HTTP 切换到 WebSocket。如以下代码片段所示：

HTTP/1.1 101 Switching Protocols
Upgrade: websocket
Connection: Upgrade
Sec-WebSocket-Accept: skjfdPPEKjdksejsl+sdr=

The server also responds with Sec-WebSocket-Accept, created by the server by appending a predefined GUID (258EAFA5-E914-47DA-95CA-C5AB0DC85B11, as defined in RFC 6455) to Sec-WebSocket-Key, hashing it to the SHA-1 algorithm and encoding it to base64.

服务器还会响应 Sec-WebSocket-Accept，它由服务器把一个预定义 GUID（258EAFA5-E914-47DA-95CA-C5AB0DC85B11，如 RFC 6455 所定义）附加到 Sec-WebSocket-Key 之后，用 SHA-1 算法哈希再做 base64 编码而成。

When the server acknowledgment is received, the WebSocket connection is established for the client and server to communicate with each other. The communication messages can be in textual or binary format following a frame structure. A frame should always be masked before sending to the server—if not, the connection is closed by the server upon receiving an unmasked frame. The masking key is 4 bytes long and should be randomly generated to mask the message payload. The masking key and payload are XOR together to generate a masked frame, and the reverse process is performed by the server to retrieve the original payload.

收到服务器确认后，WebSocket 连接即建立，客户端和服务器可以相互通信。通信消息可以是文本或二进制格式，遵循帧结构。帧在发送到服务器前必须做掩码处理——否则服务器收到未掩码的帧就会关闭连接。掩码密钥长 4 字节，应随机生成以掩码消息载荷。掩码密钥与载荷做 XOR 运算生成掩码帧，服务器再执行逆过程取回原始载荷。

The frame consists of payload data and additional metadata, such as whether the frame is masked or not (denoted by 1 or 0), payload length, and masking key. The payload data is a combination of extension data and application data. The application data consists of the original message, and extension data is an optional field that can help achieve additional capabilities, such as encryption and compression. Finally, the connection between client and server is torn down at the end of the communication.

帧由载荷数据和额外元数据组成，例如帧是否被掩码（用 1 或 0 表示）、载荷长度和掩码密钥。载荷数据由扩展数据和应用数据组合而成。应用数据就是原始消息，扩展数据是一个可选字段，可帮助实现加密和压缩等附加能力。最后，客户端与服务器之间的连接在通信结束时被拆除。

Page 174

Now, we might not always have a requirement for bidirectional connection. We may just require a communication channel from server to clients. We'll discuss this idea in the next section, where we elaborate on server-sent events (SSEs).

现在，我们并不总是需要双向连接。我们可能只需要一条从服务器到客户端的通信通道。我们将在下一节讨论这个想法，那里会详细介绍服务器发送事件（SSE）。

Push Mechanism: Server-Sent Events

Let's go back to our example of checking the status of an order we placed on an online food-ordering application. SSE can be a feasible approach in this case as the server is responsible for updating the order status and no such input is required from the client's end. The server is not dependent on any message-delivery acknowledgments from clients—if there is such a requirement, SSE might not be the best fit for that use case. SSE is implemented over a long-lived HTTP connection to consume any updates or notifications from the server in text format. We define an EventSource in a client application, which includes the URL of the SSE event stream on the server, and any new event is delivered to this EventSource via the event stream.

让我们回到在在线订餐应用上查看订单状态的例子。在这种情况下 SSE 是一种可行的方式，因为订单状态由服务器负责更新，客户端一端不需要此类输入。服务器不依赖客户端的任何消息投递确认——如果有这种需求，SSE 可能不是该用例的最佳选择。SSE 在一条长寿命 HTTP 连接上实现，以文本格式消费来自服务器的任何更新或通知。我们在客户端应用中定义一个 EventSource，它包含服务器上 SSE 事件流的 URL，任何新事件都通过事件流送达这个 EventSource。

SSE is also used in messenger applications much like WebSockets; for example, BlackBerry Messenger (BBM) and LinkedIn messaging and live video interactions work on SSE as an underlying technology.
SSE 也像 WebSocket 一样用于即时通讯应用；例如，BlackBerry Messenger（BBM）以及 LinkedIn 的消息和实时视频交互都以 SSE 作为底层技术。

We discussed that the network is not reliable in Chapter 1, and due to this unreliability, a long-lived HTTP connection can always break. In these kinds of scenarios, we need the ability to reestablish the connection from where we left off so as to continue consuming the events from the server. SSE has this capability built in: it can reestablish dropped connections and recover any messages that might have been missed by the clients during the connection issue.

我们在第 1 章讨论过网络并不可靠，正因为这种不可靠，长寿命 HTTP 连接随时可能断开。在这类场景中，我们需要能从中断处重新建立连接，以继续消费服务器的事件。SSE 内置了这种能力：它可以重新建立断开的连接，并恢复客户端在连接问题期间可能错过的任何消息。

We mentioned that responses in the case of async architectures can be delivered via WebSockets or SSE. Yet another way could be publishing a response to a topic that clients have subscribed to or delivering a response to the HTTP endpoint exposed by the client. This mechanism is widely used for server-to-server communication for callbacks (the response of the API is delivered asynchronously). We'll elaborate on this idea in Chapter 8 while discussing pub/sub architectures, and in Chapter 12 while discussing Amazon Simple Queue Service (SQS) and Amazon Simple Notification Service (SNS).

我们提到，在异步架构中响应可以通过 WebSocket 或 SSE 送达。还有一种方式是把响应发布到客户端已订阅的主题，或把响应投递到客户端暴露的 HTTP 端点。这种机制广泛用于服务器到服务器的回调通信（API 的响应异步送达）。我们将在第 8 章讨论发布/订阅架构时、以及第 12 章讨论 Amazon Simple Queue Service（SQS）和 Amazon Simple Notification Service（SNS）时详细阐述这个想法。

Up to this point, we've looked at different networking protocols and mechanisms for communication over the internet. With networking protocols, there are common communication standards (protocols or architectural styles) that are generally followed in the client-server architecture. Let's take a closer look at this.

到此为止，我们看了用于互联网通信的各种网络协议和机制。在网络协议方面，客户端-服务器架构中通常会遵循一些通用通信标准（协议或架构风格）。下面我们仔细看看。

Page 175

Common Communication Protocol Standards

In the client-server architecture, clients interact with servers to retrieve some information or perform an action on the server. Consider a scenario where each client and server defines its own paradigms for interaction over the internet—it becomes very difficult for software applications to adapt and implement a vast set of paradigms. This can be easier if the client-server calls are commonly defined and everyone uses them. In this section, we'll explain the concept of an application programming interface (API) and its multiple types to identify how they suit particular business use case requirements. An API enables two software applications to communicate over the internet using a set of definitions and protocols. We'll start our discussion with RPC and then explore other paradigms.

在客户端-服务器架构中，客户端与服务器交互以检索某些信息或在服务器上执行操作。设想这样一种场景：每个客户端和服务器都为互联网上的交互定义自己的范式——软件应用要适配和实现这一大堆范式就变得非常困难。如果客户端-服务器调用被通用定义、大家都用，事情就容易多了。在本节中，我们将解释应用程序编程接口（API）的概念及其多种类型，以识别它们如何适合特定业务用例需求。API 让两个软件应用能够使用一组定义和协议在互联网上通信。我们从 RPC 开始讨论，然后探讨其他范式。

Remote Procedure Call

Typically, a single machine can't hold all the necessary implementation logic, so part of the code is hosted somewhere else, which may or may not be owned by your company. In the example of fulfilling an order on an online food-ordering application, the frontend application calls the backend service to place an order, the backend service talks with the payment service to process the payment in the desired payment mode, the payment service talks with external providers like a bank or payment gateway (PG) to process the payment, and finally, the order is placed. Now, consider the interaction of our own payment service with a PG: the PG is not owned by us, but we invoke the payment-processing method similarly to how we call any local method in our codebase. This is referred to as Remote Procedure Call (RPC).

通常，单台机器无法容纳所有必要的实现逻辑，因此部分代码托管在别处，它可能属于你的公司、也可能不属于。以在线订餐应用履约订单为例：前端应用调用后端服务下单，后端服务与支付服务通信以按期望支付方式处理支付，支付服务再与银行或支付网关（PG）等外部提供方通信来处理支付，最后订单下成。现在考虑我们自己的支付服务与 PG 的交互：PG 并不归我们所有，但我们调用支付处理方法的方式，与调用代码库中任何本地方法类似。这就是远程过程调用（RPC）。

A procedure is a block of code responsible for executing a specific set of tasks. It can be as simple as a program adding two numbers or, in this case, processing a payment via a PG. RPC means executing this piece of code, aka the procedure, on a remote machine as if it were being executed on your local personal computer or laptop. Now, let's understand why we need such a mechanism and discuss how this remote code execution works.

过程（procedure）是负责执行一组特定任务的代码块。它可以简单到一个两数相加的程序，或者本例中通过 PG 处理支付。RPC 意味着在远程机器上执行这段代码（即过程），就像在你本地个人电脑或笔记本上执行一样。下面我们理解为什么需要这种机制，并讨论这种远程代码执行是如何工作的。

If the code is hosted on a remote machine, the one definite benefit we get is code reusability and scalability. The code can be shared among multiple clients, offering abstraction to the clients on the code execution, and it is scalable such that the code can be distributed among multiple machines. It additionally abstracts out the network communication for how the local machine interacts with the remote machine to execute a procedure; for a developer, it's similar to any local procedure call. There can be multiple teams in an organization that might own up to hundreds of microservices written in different programming languages. We define the interfaces, and RPC helps with cross-language and platform support by taking on the headache of data marshaling (encoding) and unmarshaling (decoding).

如果代码托管在远程机器上，我们获得的一个明确好处是代码复用和可扩展性。代码可以在多个客户端之间共享，对客户端屏蔽代码执行的细节，并且可扩展——代码可以分发到多台机器上。它还把本地机器如何与远程机器交互以执行过程的网络通信抽象掉；对开发者来说，这与任何本地过程调用类似。一个组织中可能有多个团队，拥有多达数百个用不同编程语言编写的微服务。我们定义接口，RPC 则通过承担数据编解码（marshaling/unmarshaling）的麻烦事来帮助实现跨语言和跨平台支持。

Page 176

Recall that while discussing the benefits of RPC, we mentioned that the different microservices might be written in different programming languages, so it's not possible to invoke the remote function directly. We need an intermediary that can handle this conversion logic—this is referred to as stub. A stub function offers a similar interface as a remote method that clients can invoke, and it internally handles the implementation details, such as network communication and marshaling of method arguments to a message over the network. On the server side, the stub function will unmarshal the message to the arguments as expected by the remote method. Once the method processing is complete, the method response is again marshaled and sent back over the network where the client-side stub function unmarshals it to an object that is readable by the client machine.

回忆一下，在讨论 RPC 的好处时我们提到，不同微服务可能用不同编程语言编写，因此无法直接调用远程函数。我们需要一个能处理这种转换逻辑的中介——这就是 stub（存根）。stub 函数提供与远程方法类似的接口供客户端调用，它在内部处理实现细节，例如网络通信以及把方法参数编组为网络上的消息。在服务器端，stub 函数把消息反编组为远程方法期望的参数。方法处理完成后，方法响应再次被编组并通过网络发回，客户端侧的 stub 函数把它反编组为客户端机器可读的对象。

The common interface or a contract to specify the remote procedures and data types is defined in the interface definition language (IDL). This interface is language agnostic, meaning it will work with any desired programming language. The IDL is used to generate the stubs used for client communication. Some examples include the Web Services Description Language (WSDL), which is used with Simple Object Access Protocol (SOAP), and the Apache Thrift IDL.

用于指定远程过程和数据类型的通用接口或契约，用接口定义语言（IDL）定义。这个接口与语言无关，意味着它适用于任何想要的编程语言。IDL 用于生成客户端通信所用的 stub。一些例子包括与简单对象访问协议（SOAP）配合使用的 Web 服务描述语言（WSDL），以及 Apache Thrift IDL。

While there are benefits to RPC, there are also downsides since we're operating in a distributed environment. Some of the issues we might face here, which we don't have to consider with local method invocation, are worrying about network latency, handling network failures and retry mechanisms for network calls, and ensuring the interfaces are compatible as systems evolve.

虽然 RPC 有好处，但由于我们在分布式环境中运作，它也有缺点。这里可能遇到一些本地方法调用时不必考虑的问题：担心网络延迟、处理网络故障和网络调用的重试机制、以及随着系统演进确保接口兼容。

Some examples of RPC include SOAP, Representational State Transfer (REST), gRPC, and Thrift. SOAP is a protocol that offers mechanisms to clients and servers for communicating with one another using XML messages. SOAP is not tied to any specific protocol and can be used alongside other protocols, such as HTTP, SMTP, and TCP, although it is mostly used with HTTP. SOAP is relatively complex with its XML-based structure, and it has its own learning curve. You won't find many new use cases being developed via this protocol. Developers tend to lean toward simpler paradigms, such as REST, over SOAP for application development and interaction over the internet.

RPC 的一些例子包括 SOAP、表述性状态转移（REST）、gRPC 和 Thrift。SOAP 是一种协议，它为客户端和服务器提供使用 XML 消息相互通信的机制。SOAP 不绑定任何特定协议，可以与 HTTP、SMTP 和 TCP 等其他协议一起使用，尽管它主要与 HTTP 配合。SOAP 基于 XML 的结构相对复杂，有自己的学习曲线。你不会看到很多新用例通过这个协议开发。在互联网上做应用开发和交互时，开发者倾向于 REST 等更简单的范式而非 SOAP。

REST

REST is widely used alongside the HTTP protocol for client-server interactions and uses HTTP methods to implement different CRUD (create, read, update, and delete) operations. REST is a software architectural style, not a protocol like SOAP, and is used extensively for building applications for today's internet.

REST 与 HTTP 协议一起广泛用于客户端-服务器交互，并使用 HTTP 方法实现不同的 CRUD（创建、读取、更新、删除）操作。REST 是一种软件架构风格，不是像 SOAP 那样的协议，被广泛用于构建当今互联网的应用。

Page 177

The following are the guiding principles of the REST design pattern:

以下是 REST 设计模式的指导原则：

  • Communication over REST APIs includes the clients, the server, and resources. The resource is a fundamental entity that can be uniquely identified by a URL. The clients can interact with the server to perform any operation on these resources via HTTP methods.
    基于 REST API 的通信包括客户端、服务器和资源。资源是可以由 URL 唯一标识的基本实体。客户端可以与服务器交互，通过 HTTP 方法对这些资源执行任意操作。
  • REST operates over a stateless paradigm, meaning the server is not responsible for maintaining the state of older requests. The state maintenance (if required) should be handled by the client, and all relevant information should be part of the HTTP request in order for the server to process it.
    REST 运行在无状态范式上，意味着服务器不负责维护旧请求的状态。状态维护（如果需要）应由客户端处理，所有相关信息都应作为 HTTP 请求的一部分，以便服务器处理。
  • It is possible that responses to particular REST APIs don't change too frequently. In these kinds of scenarios, the responses can be cached at the client's end, at the browser level, or using a CDN or any other caching mechanism.
    对某些 REST API 的响应可能不常变化。在这类场景中，响应可以缓存在客户端一端、浏览器层面，或使用 CDN 或任何其他缓存机制。
  • There is a uniform interface between the components involved in information transfer following standardized ways for communication. This ensures that it's easy to evolve the capability of the software application. Key factors include unique resource identification, resource update via representations (the client and server communicate to update a resource in formats such as plain text, JSON, XML, or HTML), self-descriptive messages (the server should share relevant information in response in order for it to be processed by the client), and hypermedia as the engine of application state (clients should be able to navigate through the resources via hyperlinks present in the server response).
    参与信息传递的各组件之间遵循标准化通信方式，有一个统一接口。这确保软件应用的能力易于演进。关键因素包括：资源唯一标识、通过表示更新资源（客户端和服务器以纯文本、JSON、XML 或 HTML 等格式通信以更新资源）、自描述消息（服务器应在响应中分享相关信息以便客户端处理）、以及超媒体作为应用状态引擎（客户端应能通过服务器响应中的超链接在资源间导航）。
  • Multiple systems can be involved in gathering information. The client is abstracted out from these multiple layer calls inside the system and is only responsible for sending requests to the first layer (such as an LB, API gateway, or any other service endpoint) and gathering a response from it.
    收集信息可能涉及多个系统。客户端被从系统内部的多层调用中抽象出来，只负责向第一层（例如 LB、API 网关或任何其他服务端点）发送请求并从中收集响应。
  • The server can deliver code on demand in the form of scripts in response to client requests, and clients can execute it per requirement.
    服务器可以按需以脚本形式响应客户端请求交付代码，客户端可以按需执行。

Note that the APIs following these standards are referred to as RESTful APIs.

注意，遵循这些标准的 API 称为 RESTful API。

We'll explore LBs, API gateways, NAT, IP addresses, and related networking concepts in Chapter 9.
我们将在第 9 章探讨 LB、API 网关、NAT、IP 地址及相关网络概念。

As REST can operate with JSON, it's simple for developers to work with. SOAP is known for its support for advanced security features, typed data, and procedures (SOAP allows RPCs similar to local procedures), but it comes with higher complexity. We can definitely introduce advanced security aspects in REST as well, though that

由于 REST 可以用 JSON 工作，开发者用起来很简单。SOAP 以支持高级安全特性、带类型数据和过程（SOAP 允许类似本地过程的 RPC）而著称，但它复杂度更高。我们当然也可以在 REST 中引入高级安全方面，不过那

Page 178

requires extra design considerations that SOAP is inherently built to support. As always, it varies from use case to use case, and there is no perfect choice.

需要额外的设计考量，而 SOAP 天生就是为支持这些而构建的。一如既往，这因用例而异，没有完美选择。

The REST architectural pattern operates on a fixed schema defined by the server, but in some cases, we might look for flexibility in the way that the client can define data needs. Let's explore this idea in more detail in the next section where we talk about GraphQL.

REST 架构模式运行在服务器定义的固定 schema 上，但在某些情况下，我们可能希望在客户端定义数据需求的方式上有灵活性。下一节我们详细探讨这个想法，谈谈 GraphQL。

GraphQL

GraphQL is an API query language that allows clients to write a query specific to data retrieved on a single API endpoint (unlike REST, where we define endpoints per API). To compare GraphQL with REST, let's look at an example: we want to retrieve a food item's name and description to show items that are available from a particular restaurant on an online food-ordering application. With REST, we'll require an API that can return these exact details or use an API that returns complete information about the food item and shows only the required information on the application (similarly, there can be cases where we need to combine data from multiple APIs).

GraphQL 是一种 API 查询语言，它允许客户端在单个 API 端点上编写针对所检索数据的查询（不像 REST 那样为每个 API 定义端点）。为了把 GraphQL 与 REST 比较，我们看一个例子：我们想检索一个食品条目的名称和描述，以在在线订餐应用上展示某家餐厅可供的菜品。用 REST 时，我们需要一个能返回这些精确细节的 API，或者用一个返回食品条目完整信息的 API、然后在应用上只显示所需信息（类似地，有时我们需要组合来自多个 API 的数据）。

There can be scenarios of overfetching or underfetching data with REST, which can be resolved by the query flexibility offered by GraphQL, in addition to a few other features that we'll discuss shortly. Querying only the required data consumes only the necessary network bandwidth, which can make applications faster on slower networks.

使用 REST 可能出现过度获取或获取不足数据的场景，GraphQL 提供的查询灵活性可以解决这些问题，此外还有一些其他特性我们稍后讨论。只查询所需数据只消耗必要的网络带宽，这能让应用在较慢网络上更快。

Now that you have a fair idea of GraphQL's advantages over REST, let's dig a little deeper into how it works. GraphQL has a strong type system to define the entities supported via the client's query, which are written in the GraphQL Schema Definition Language (SDL). Let's extend our previous example to show how it can be supported via GraphQL:

现在你对 GraphQL 相比 REST 的优势有了相当了解，让我们更深入一点看看它如何工作。GraphQL 有一个强大的类型系统来定义客户端查询所支持的实体，这些实体用 GraphQL Schema 定义语言（SDL）编写。让我们扩展前面的例子，展示如何通过 GraphQL 支持：

type Restaurant {
  id: String!
  name: String!
  rating: Float
  foodItems: [FoodItem!]!
}

type FoodItem {
  id: String!
  name: String!
  rating: Float
  isVeg: Boolean!
}

query {
  Restaurant (id: "lsoa34444lsoa") {
    name
    foodItems {
      name
Page 179
      description
    }
  }
}

We defined two objects in SDL to support our example: Restaurant and FoodItem (the exclamation mark [!] denotes a mandatory attribute). To gather data on food items, the query specifies only the attributes required by the client.

我们在 SDL 中定义了两个对象来支持例子：Restaurant 和 FoodItem（感叹号 [!] 表示必填属性）。为了收集食品条目数据，查询只指定客户端所需的属性。

Visit the GraphQL documentation for full information on GraphQL.
请访问 GraphQL 文档以了解 GraphQL 的完整信息。

Moving forward, querying (data read) is not the only capability we need with the APIs; we also need support for operations such as creating, updating, and deleting data (data modification on server data stores). GraphQL supports these operations with a feature called mutations. The mutations start with a mutation keyword with syntax similar to GraphQL queries. Let's look at an example mutation of creating a new food item for a restaurant:

继续说，查询（数据读取）并不是我们对 API 唯一需要的能力；我们还需要支持创建、更新和删除数据（对服务器数据存储的数据修改）等操作。GraphQL 用一个称为 mutation（变更）的特性支持这些操作。mutations 以 mutation 关键字开头，语法与 GraphQL 查询类似。下面看一个为餐厅创建新食品条目的 mutation 例子：

mutation {
  createFoodItem(name: "Paneer Tikka Masala", isVeg: true) {
    id
    name
  }
}

Mutations can also send a response similar to a GraphQL query. Along with performing its main job of data modification, as in the previous example, the mutation will return the ID and name of the newly created food item as part of the response.

Mutations 也可以发送类似 GraphQL 查询的响应。除了执行数据修改这一主要工作（如前例），mutation 还会在响应中返回新创建食品条目的 ID 和名称。

We might also be interested in knowing about any new changes happening on the server side. For this, we can leverage technologies such as SSE or WebSockets, which we discussed earlier in this chapter. We can also use GraphQL subscriptions (defined by the Subscription keyword), which inherently establish a bidirectional connection to inform us about any new events in near real time, such as if a new food item is created. GraphQL queries, mutations, and subscriptions are defined in the GraphQL schema and offer clients insights into the API capabilities.

我们可能还想了解服务器端发生的任何新变化。为此，我们可以利用本章前面讨论过的 SSE 或 WebSocket 等技术。我们也可以使用 GraphQL subscription（由 Subscription 关键字定义），它本质上建立一条双向连接，近实时地告知我们任何新事件，例如是否创建了新食品条目。GraphQL 查询、mutation 和 subscription 都定义在 GraphQL schema 中，向客户端展示 API 能力。

One of the benefits of GraphQL over REST is its integration with a single endpoint and the fact that it serves all the API needs with the same API endpoint, instead of multiple endpoints. As our system evolves, it's possible that frontend applications will need to interact with multiple backend applications to gather the necessary data, and each backend application exposes its own GraphQL endpoint. This can be optimized

GraphQL 相比 REST 的一个好处是它与单个端点集成，用同一个 API 端点（而非多个端点）满足所有 API 需求。随着系统演进，前端应用可能需要与多个后端应用交互以收集必要数据，而每个后端应用都暴露自己的 GraphQL 端点。这可以被优化

Page 180

by choosing a GraphQL client like Apollo or AWS AppSync (which we'll discuss in Chapter 12) to help applications scale with much more ease.

方法是选择 Apollo 或 AWS AppSync（我们将在第 12 章讨论）这样的 GraphQL 客户端，以帮助应用更轻松地扩展。

Web Real-Time Communication

People around the world interact with one another over text messaging, voice calls, or video calls. Text messaging is simple to implement and operate compared to voice and video calls. Think of a scenario where you're interacting with your friend on a video call: what do you expect experience-wise from the video-calling application? The primary expectations are that you're able to see your friend clearly and to hear their voice without any lag. WebRTC (which stands for Web Real-Time Communication) offers a mechanism for supporting audio and video communications in web browsers or mobile applications by APIs without requiring installation of any specific plug-ins. It also offers support for file sharing and data exchange between the web services in near real time.

世界各地的人们通过文本消息、语音通话或视频通话相互交流。与语音和视频通话相比，文本消息的实现和运营都更简单。设想你正在与朋友视频通话的场景：你对视频通话应用的体验有什么期待？主要期待是能清楚地看到朋友、毫无延迟地听到他们的声音。WebRTC（即 Web 实时通信）提供了一种机制，通过 API 在网页浏览器或移动应用中支持音频和视频通信，而无需安装任何特定插件。它还支持在 Web 服务之间近实时地共享文件和交换数据。

Up to this point, all the protocols or architectural patterns we've discussed have included a server, and we focused our discussion on client-server communication. WebRTC allows direct peer-to-peer connection without any requirement for a server in between. Even though peers can communicate directly, a server can be introduced if the need arises (such as to ensure secure communication). A key consideration to note is that the latency can increase substantially if the number of peers communicating with one another increases to double digits—for example, a voice channel on Discord servers with a thousand members.

到此为止，我们讨论的所有协议或架构模式都包含一台服务器，我们的讨论聚焦于客户端-服务器通信。WebRTC 允许直接的点对点连接，中间不需要服务器。尽管对等方可以直接通信，但如果需要（例如为确保安全通信），也可以引入服务器。需要注意的一个关键考量是：如果相互通信的对等方数量增加到两位数，延迟可能大幅上升——例如 Discord 服务器上有一千名成员的语音频道。

WebRTC is not itself a protocol—it's a tool working on top of multiple protocols to serve our use case. Some APIs offered by WebRTC include RTCPeerConnection for establishing connections between the peers, getUserMedia to access audio and video from a user's device, and RTCDataChannel for bidirectional data exchange between the peers. Let's take a look at how the peer-to-peer connection is established.

WebRTC 本身不是协议——它是一个工作在多个协议之上、服务我们用例的工具。WebRTC 提供的一些 API 包括：在对等方之间建立连接的 RTCPeerConnection、从用户设备访问音频和视频的 getUserMedia，以及在对等方之间双向数据交换的 RTCDataChannel。下面我们看看点对点连接是如何建立的。

For communication over the internet and connecting with another device, we require the IP address and the port number. It becomes difficult if the devices are behind a NAT (more details on this in Chapter 9). In these kinds of scenarios, WebRTC can use Interactive Connectivity Establishment (ICE), which helps figure out the optimal communication route. We don't require ICE if it is not a direct peer-to-peer connection and our system operates on a client-server architecture.

要在互联网上通信并连接另一台设备，我们需要 IP 地址和端口号。如果设备位于 NAT 之后就会变得困难（第 9 章详述）。在这类场景中，WebRTC 可以使用交互式连接建立（ICE），它帮助找出最优通信路由。如果不是直接点对点连接、而我们的系统运行在客户端-服务器架构上，就不需要 ICE。

To communicate with any device, we need a unique address. This might not be possible if you're operating inside a private network behind a NAT (all devices in this network will have the same public IP address and are distinguished by assigned private IP address). The Session Traversal Utilities for NAT (STUN) protocol is used if the devices are behind a NAT. Both the peers connect with the STUN server to figure out the IP address, port (allocated by NAT corresponding to the private IP address and port), and type of NAT the device is behind. Once this information is

要与任何设备通信，我们需要一个唯一地址。如果你在 NAT 后的私有网络内操作，这可能无法实现（该网络中的所有设备都有相同的公网 IP 地址，通过分配的私有 IP 地址区分）。如果设备位于 NAT 之后，就使用 NAT 会话穿越应用程序（STUN）协议。两个对等方都与 STUN 服务器连接，以弄清 IP 地址、端口（由 NAT 对应私有 IP 地址和端口分配）以及设备所在 NAT 的类型。一旦这些信息

Page 181

obtained, it will be used as part of the Session Description Protocol (SDP), as shown in Figure 6-4.

获得，它将作为会话描述协议（SDP）的一部分使用，如图 6-4 所示。

The two peer devices exchange ICE candidates (network address and port) with each other via a signaling mechanism such as SDP. SDP includes information like media type (audio or video), transport protocol (UDP, IP, etc.), media format, remote address, and port for the media.

两台对等设备通过 SDP 这样的信令机制相互交换 ICE candidate（网络地址和端口）。SDP 包含媒体类型（音频或视频）、传输协议（UDP、IP 等）、媒体格式、远端地址和媒体端口等信息。

In some scenarios, direct peer-to-peer connection may not be feasible because of restrictive firewalls and the STUN server fails to do its job. In these scenarios, we can use Traversal Using Relays around NAT (TURN) servers. A TURN server acts as an intermediary between the peers to communicate, where essentially one device sends a message to the TURN server, and then the TURN server relays this to another device. A TURN server can be used singlehandedly to serve the functionality of STUN and relay traffic, but the STUN server is always used as the first point of action. This is because using the TURN server to stream high-quality data is relatively expensive, adding an extra hop into the architecture.

在某些场景中，由于防火墙限制，直接点对点连接可能不可行，STUN 服务器也无法完成工作。在这些场景中，我们可以使用 NAT 中继穿越（TURN）服务器。TURN 服务器充当对等方之间通信的中介，本质上一台设备把消息发给 TURN 服务器，然后 TURN 服务器把它中继到另一台设备。TURN 服务器可以单独使用来同时承担 STUN 的功能和中继流量，但 STUN 服务器总是作为第一选择。这是因为用 TURN 服务器流式传输高质量数据相对昂贵，会在架构中增加一跳。

Once the peer-to-peer connection is established, media data can be exchanged in both directions to carry forward the communication. WebRTC is used across the IT industry to support voice and video communications.

点对点连接建立后，媒体数据可以双向交换以继续通信。WebRTC 被整个 IT 行业用于支持语音和视频通信。

Conclusion

The OSI model is a good starting point for understanding data communication over the internet. The device communications we see around us mostly follow the TCP/IP model, with TCP, UDP, and IP being the base protocols for data transport. Multiple protocols are built around them, such as HTTP, SMTP, and XMPP, to serve specific

OSI 模型是理解互联网上数据通信的良好起点。我们周围看到的设备通信大多遵循 TCP/IP 模型，TCP、UDP 和 IP 是数据传输的基础协议。围绕它们构建了多个协议，例如 HTTP、SMTP 和 XMPP，以服务特定

Page 182

use cases. Determining which protocol makes more sense to implement for your specific use case can be confusing, so it's important to identify the most critical requirements to make your decision. You may also find that combining multiple technologies to meet customer demands is your best option. For example, XMPP is extensively used for text messages, and WebRTC is a preferred choice for audio and video communications. Direct peer-to-peer communication can become complex, particularly when you involve multiuser experiences such as group video or audio calls. Combining these tools can reduce this complexity, bringing the benefits of the text, audio, and video functionality of WebRTC and XMPP together.

用例。为你的特定用例决定实现哪种协议更合理可能令人困惑，因此识别最关键的需求来做决定很重要。你也可能发现组合多种技术来满足客户需求才是最佳选择。例如，XMPP 广泛用于文本消息，WebRTC 是音频和视频通信的首选。直接点对点通信可能变得复杂，尤其是当你涉及群组视频或音频通话等多用户体验时。组合这些工具可以降低这种复杂性，把 WebRTC 和 XMPP 的文本、音频和视频功能优势结合起来。

We also discussed communication types and which mechanism might make more sense for your implementation. We suggest having your use case requirements in place before trying to compare your options—there may never be a clear winner when designing large-scale distributed systems. We ended our discussion with different communication standards and architectures for how client-server information sharing works across the internet. While we have tried to cover the basic and most widely used communication tools, multiple other protocols or technologies have been designed and built to solve specific use cases that we simply didn't have the room to discuss here.

我们还讨论了通信类型以及哪种机制可能更适合你的实现。我们建议在比较各选项之前先把用例需求定下来——在设计大规模分布式系统时，可能永远没有明确的赢家。我们以客户端-服务器信息共享如何跨互联网运作的不同通信标准和架构结束了讨论。虽然我们试图涵盖基本的、最广泛使用的通信工具，但还有许多其他协议或技术被设计和构建出来解决特定用例，只是这里没有篇幅讨论。

In the next chapter we'll dig into the concept of containers. Docker and Kubernetes are hot keywords in the industry—it's likely you've already heard of these concepts, which are used to deploy and run your software applications.

下一章我们将深入容器的概念。Docker 和 Kubernetes 是行业里的热词——你很可能已经听说过这些概念，它们用于部署和运行你的软件应用。
